arxiv-2011-11357.creator: Yuewen Zhu, Chunran Zheng, Chongjian Yuan, Xu Huang, Xiaoping Hong
arxiv-2011-11357.description: Abstract Combining lidar in camera-based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) is an effective method in improving overall accuracy, especially at a large scale outdoor scenario. Recent development of low-cost lidars (e.g. Livox lidar) enable us to explore such SLAM systems with lower budget and higher performance.

arxiv-2409-04266.title: Dual balanced readout for scattered light noise mitigation in Michelson interferometers
arxiv-2409-04266.creator: André Lohde, Daniel Voigt, Oliver Gerberding
arxiv-2409-04266.description: Abstract Ground-based gravitational wave detectors use laser interferometry to detect the minuscule distance change between test masses caused by gravitational waves. Stray light that scatters back into the interferometer causes transient signals that can cover the same frequency range as a potential gravitational wave signal.

arxiv-2602-03213.creator: Zhuoran Yang, Yanyong Zhang
arxiv-2602-03213.description: Abstract Autonomous driving relies on robust models trained on large-scale, high-quality multi-view driving videos. pmc-11642327.title: Comparison of the Effects of Ultrasound-Guided Subacromial Injection Versus Subacromial Injection and Suprascapular Nerve Block on Pain, Function, and Sleep Quality in Rotator Cuff Lesions
pmc-11642327.creator: Mustafa Haciomeroglu, Suna Akin Takmaz, Azize Serce, Yilmaz Karaduman, Hulya Basar, Mariateresa Giglio
pmc-11642327.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: Rotator cuff lesions are common causes of shoulder pain. When not treated effectively, the functional loss associated with pain affects the quality of life and brings about psychosocial issues. In this study, prospective observational comparison of the effects of ultrasonography (USG) guided subacromial injection (SAI) versus subacromial injection combined with suprascapular nerve block (SSNB) on pain, functionality and sleep quality in the treatment of shoulder pain unresponsive to conservative treatments due to rotator cuff lesions is made.

pmc-11669522.title: Functional interaction of melatonin with gasotransmitters and ROS in plant adaptation to abiotic stresses
pmc-11669522.creator: Yuriy E. Kolupaev, Alla Yemets, Tetiana O. Yastreb, Yaroslav Blume
pmc-11669522.description: Melatonin is considered a multifunctional stress metabolite and a novel plant hormone affecting seed germination, root architecture, circadian rhythms, leaf senescence, and fruit ripening. Melatonin functions related to plant adaptation to stress stimuli of various natures are considered especially important.

pmc-11679556.title: Light-Emitting Diode Array with Optical Linear Detector Enables High-Throughput Differential Single-Cell Dielectrophoretic Analysis
pmc-11679556.creator: Emerich Kovacs, Behnam Arzang, Elham Salimi, Michael Butler, Greg E Bridges, Douglas J Thomson, Arunas Ramanavicius
pmc-11679556.description: This paper presents a lens-free imaging approach utilizing an array of light sources, capable of measuring the dielectric properties of many particles simultaneously. This method employs coplanar electrodes to induce velocity changes in flowing particles through dielectrophoretic forces, allowing the inference of individual particle properties from differential velocity changes. Both positive and negative forces are detectable.

AimsAutoscopic phenomena (AP) are distinct manifestations of epileptic seizure semiology and are also identified in diverse psychiatric disorders. pmc-13058485.title: Nurturing others neglecting self: A qualitative study on work-life balance among nurse educators at a Gauteng nursing education institution
pmc-13058485.creator: Letta Mathebula, Rirhandzu F. Mathevula, Tshiamo N. Ramalepa
pmc-13058485.description: BackgroundNurse educators are instrumental in preparing the next generation of nurses. However, the changing landscape of nursing education is making it difficult for them to exemplify and advocate for work-life balance (WLB). pmc-13374675.title: Therapeutic Potential of Alternating Magnetic Fields for Normalizing Blood Parameters and Restoring Renal, and Cardiac Function in Diabetic Mice
pmc-13374675.creator: Mokhamad Tirono, Farid Samsu Hananto
pmc-13374675.description: Background:In recent years, the number of adults aged 20–79 years living with diabetes has increased more than threefold. Currently, the treatment of diabetes typically involves the long-term use of chemical and herbal drugs. pmc-13588313.title: Isatin derivatives as potent cholinesterase inhibitors: recent developments and future challenges
pmc-13588313.creator: Muhammad Shahzad, Alia Mushtaq, Christophe Rochais, Muhammad Moazzam Naseer
pmc-13588313.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline, memory impairment, and neuronal loss, primarily associated with β-amyloid plaque deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, and cholinergic dysfunction. Since the disruption of cholinergic neurotransmission is a key pathological feature of AD, the cholinesterase (ChE) inhibitors targeting acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) remain the mainstay of symptomatic treatment by enhancing synaptic acetylcholine levels.

pmc-13626460.title: Strategic Inversion: How Refugees Reconfigure Everyday Resistance under Benevolent Oppression
pmc-13626460.creator: Rekha Krishnan, Aloysius Marcus Kahindi, Rajiv Krishnan Kozhikode
pmc-13626460.description: What does everyday resistance look like among dominated populations experiencing paternalistic care rather than extraction? Research on everyday resistance emerged from contexts where power extracts surplus from the oppressed. In this scholarship, the backstage is a space where the dominated cultivate hidden transcripts to cope with oppression, while the frontstage, where performances are enacted to those in power, is primary.
